item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Ha! This! ^

I just read ALL the comments because I wanted to see if someone had already pointed this out, because it's really odd! And then most of the comments instead state how amazing the writing is.

Maybe it's cause the original image is gone (though I agree that images alone shouldn't make or break skips), maybe I'm just weird, but this really does not excite me at all. (Haven't read the Addendums yet, not really motivated, but gonna force myself to give this thing another chance, there has to be a reason it got so many votes.)

I find the writing not up to the clinical standards I expect from the Foundation. The quote above is part of that. Also, that weird redaction of the numbers before giving exact percentages. And I also find the redactions of the locations really weird an inconsistant and "imprecise", mostly. Examples:

high school drama performance in █████████████, ████.

High school is afaik an American concept / term.

elaboration:
+ show block
– hide block

I'm German. We don't have "high schools". I've worked as a translator, so I am very familiar with how that term is often chosen as a simplified concept, but it misses the mark. Now, I don't have the time right now to do extensive research about how this is handled around the world, but just look at Britain, there are no "high schools" there as well. The term "high school" is inherently American to me (and I would say to lots of people around the world.) It's not incorrect, per se, but it's just not precise enough for my taste. Actually, the term "high school drama" makes it even more American.

Anyway, the point is, I take this to hint at a location inside the US. Which would mean that there would need to be an additional ", ███".

+ show block
– hide block

Later on, there is these passages, adding to the inconsistencies:

during a performance of the play in ██████, ██, USA.

performance at a small theater in ██████, ███, ██;

I can't make anything of this format. (City, State, Nation) to me is a distinctly northern American format. But I'm not going to research that now, might be I am just unaware of this format commonly used elsewhere. Therefore, it's confusing to me that the state consists of 3 expunged letters and the nation only of two. Should be vice versa, in my understanding.

performance at the University of ███████████, ███████████, ███████;

Again, this just seems American to me. There is no "University of Berlin", Berlin, Germany" or anything I can make sense of that would make sense. Maybe I'm missing something else though, I don't know how they do it in Australia or elsewhere around the globe.

██ performance at ██████ University

just completely breaks the format

performance by a student group in ███████, CA

inconsistant as well

the 19██ incident in ██████████████, OH, USA

again, inconsistant

All these hints towards a mostly American context make the following sentence weirdly stand out:

Strangely, the text does not appear in the Stationers’ Register.

This strongly suggests a British origin that I feel wasn't properly set up in the rest of the skip. And yes, I did see that its first version is from before the US were a thing and the reference to Cambridge. This might be something I am reading into it personally though, just putting it here for further information.

Anyway, I feel like this is getting to wordy. I still have more criticism though, good and bad. I'm just gonna put it here quickly.

  1. spontaneously appearing items should be elaborated upon further.
  2. unclear how it is known
  3. the entire part regarding the first 1-2 weeks prior to the play confuses me. How did they find that out? It's rehearsals, so it's not like there is a lot of people that aren't involved around.
  4. I think the subtle little hint at "the forefront of an invasion scenario" is great and should be fleshed out. (I'm assuming this happens in the Addendums.)

The Ambassador of Alagadda is also to be found in the article for SCP 2264 a portal to a land of the same name, serving under a "hanged king". This hanged king has a GoI entry Here: http://wanderers-library.wikidot.com/thearchivistslog , and a word mentioned in the 2264 article is "Neverwere", another GoI on the same page.

The Agent interviewed in collapsable 3 in the SCP 2264 article, says the hanged kings face was a "God shaped hole"

Agent Alexander Papadopoulos: [emotionless] A god shaped hole. The barren desolation of a fallen and failed creation. You see the light of long dead stars. Your existence is nothing but an echo of a dying god's screams. The unseen converges. Surrounds you. And it tightens like a noose

In addition to containing the word noose, this is a term spoken by a towns man in a interview found in SCP 2480, a sarkic SCP.

Man was delirious by the end. Said the town had a "god-shaped hole" in it. Couldn't get him to elaborate.

I believe that SCP 701-1, the Ambassador, is actually Grand Karcist Ion.
